title: Computer-designed proteins neutralize snake toxins
summary: Small, stable proteins designed with AI bind and neutralize three-finger toxins from cobras and mambas in the lab; in mice, they yield 80–100% survival against lethal neurotoxin doses, depending on the toxin. Laboratory and animal studies only; traditional antivenoms remain central.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Lab tests showed the designed proteins neutralized multiple subtypes of three-finger toxins; in mice they gave complete protection from lethal neurotoxin exposure, with 80-100% survival depending on the toxin and antitoxin.
evidence.unknown: The page does not mention human trials, toxin types other than elapid three-finger toxins, and traditional antivenoms remain central to treatment.
evidence.ai_role: Designed small, stable proteins on the computer that bind key regions of the toxins.
